info.description:
# Introduction [Rabbiit](https://www.rabbiit.com) is a time tracking and project management software for teams and freelancers, built to make time management simple, fast, and accurate.

The Rabbiit API is a RESTful web service that enables full integration with your workspace. It accepts JSON (`application/json`) and form-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) request bodies, returns JSON responses, and uses standard HTTP methods, authentication, and status codes. The examples in this documentation use JSON.

### Base URL ```https://app.rabbiit.com/api/v1```

### Sending data - **GET** reads data. It lists resources or fetches one resource by ID. It does not change anything. - **POST** creates or updates a resource. - When creating, send the required fields, such as `name` or `email`. The other fields are optional. - When updating, send only the attributes you want to change. Anything you omit stays as it is. - **DELETE** removes a resource. Sending back the full object from a GET also writes every writable field in that body. On an update, send only what should change. ### How to archive records Archiving updates only the record itself. Related records stay as they are and the full history remains. Send only `active` set to `0`. The record can be reactivated at any time by sending `active` set to `1`. Archive user `15`: `POST /users/15` ```json { "active": 0 } ``` Archive project `449`: `POST /projects/449` ```json { "active": 0 } ```

# Authentication Send your **personal API token** on every request in the HTTP header `x-api-token`.

Personal tokens are created inside the Rabbiit app, while you are logged in. They are not created by sending an email and password to the API.

A personal token has the same access as the user who created it. Keep it secret. Do not commit it to GitHub, ship it in client-side code, or share it in public channels.

Personal tokens are not tied to a User-Agent and do not expire after 30 days of inactivity. Revoke a token from the app when an integration should stop working. ## Create a personal token 1. Sign in at [app.rabbiit.com](https://app.rabbiit.com). 2. Open the account menu and go to **Settings**. 3. In the **You** section, open **My tokens** (`#/personal-tokens`). 4. Choose **New token** and give it a name that identifies the integration, such as `ERP integration`. 5. Copy the token immediately. For security, Rabbiit shows the full value only once. The account administrator controls who can create tokens (**Administrators only**, **Administrators and super users**, or **All members**) under **Settings > Integrations > API management**. Administrators can review and revoke every token in the account under **Settings > Integrations > Account tokens**. ## Deprecated login Stop using email and password to authenticate with the API. `POST /auth` is deprecated. Use a **personal token**. It is secure, more flexible, and managed in the app under **Settings > You > My tokens**. The token created with email and password has a time limit and is tied to the browser user agent. New integrations are no longer accepted through this path. Integrations that already use this login can continue until **April 30, 2027**. After that date, this access stops working.

# Errors The Rabbiit API follows standard [HTTP status codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_HTTP_status_codes) to indicate whether a request was successful or failed. - **2xx** — The request was successful, and the response contains the expected data. - **4xx** — The request failed due to invalid input, missing parameters, or authentication errors. The response body usually includes a message explaining the issue. - **5xx** — A server-side error occurred while processing the request. These are unexpected and typically temporary. Each error response includes a clear message and, when applicable, an error code to help identify and handle the problem programmatically.

# Rate Limit Rabbiit API enforces multiple rate-limit layers to ensure fair usage and consistent performance. These combined mechanisms guarantee stability for all tenants while allowing higher-tier accounts to scale safely. All rate limits described below may be adjusted at any time based on system performance or usage behavior. Integrators are responsible for implementing safeguards to prevent service interruption by monitoring the `Retry-After` header and applying automatic backoff or retry logic when limits are reached. ### **Available Limits** - **Authentication Limit** — per user - **Per-Token Limit (per minute)** — per API token - **Per-Account Daily Limit** — shared by all users and tokens within the same account - **Per-IP Limit (global)** — applies to all incoming requests regardless of authentication ### **Authentication Limit** The deprecated email-and-password login (`POST /auth`) is limited to **60 requests per day per user**, to reduce brute-force attempts. Personal tokens are created in the app and do not use that endpoint. If the deprecated login limit is exceeded, the API returns **HTTP 429 Too Many Requests** or, in some cases, **HTTP 401 Unauthorized**. ### **Per-Token Limit (per minute)** Each API token has its own short-term quota of **600 requests per minute**, with a burst capacity of **30 requests per second**. These limits prevent excessive concurrent usage from a single integration. Different tokens will have independent limits. If the limit is exceeded, the API returns **HTTP 429 Too Many Requests** and includes an `minute_limit_exceeded` or `second_limit_exceeded` error in response. ### **Per-Account Daily Limit** Each account has a **single daily quota shared across all its users and tokens**, according to the subscribed plan: The quota in force for an account is the plan limit. Current usage, remaining requests, and the reset time are shown in the app under **Settings > Integrations > API management**. | Plan | Daily Limit | |--------------------------------------|----------------------------------------| | **Free / Free Trial / Legacy plans** | 50 requests per day | | **Plus** | 1 000 requests per day | | **Ultimate** | 2 500 requests per day | | **Business** | 5 000 requests per day (soft limit\*) | | **Business Max** | 25 000 requests per day (soft limit\*) | If the limit is exceeded, the API returns **HTTP 429 Too Many Requests** and includes an `account_daily_limit_exceeded` error in response. \* **Business plans** operate under a soft limit — requests beyond this threshold are temporarily accepted, but a warning is returned. For consistent overuse, an **add-on** is recommended to expand the daily quota. ### **Per-IP Limit (general)** Additionally, all incoming traffic is protected by a global network limit of **2 000 requests per minute per IP address**, independent of authentication. If the limit is exceeded, the API returns **HTTP 429 Too Many Requests** and includes an `ip_rate_limit_exceeded` error in response. ### **Rate Limit Headers** | Header | Description | |--------|--------------| | **X-RateLimit-Minute** | Minute-based limit for the current token (limit, used, remaining, reset) | | **X-RateLimit-AccountDaily** | Daily limit for the entire account (limit, used, remaining, reset) | | **X-RateLimit-AccountDaily-Warning** | Indicates when the daily quota has been exceeded — possible values:
• `soft_limit_exceeded`: soft limit reached (temporary allowance for Business plans)
• `hard_limit_blocked`: hard block applied (requests rejected) | | **Retry-After** | Returned with **HTTP 429 Too Many Requests** — specifies how many seconds to wait before retrying; |

Start date for new rate.

only_admin_see_others.description: Deprecated. Still accepted on save and not returned. Use `todo_permissions` instead.

total_members.description: A integer that represents total of active project members in the project

value_total.description: A integer that represents billable amount in the project

todo_permissions.description: Who can perform each to-do action on this project. `member_visibility` is `all_activities` or `assigned_only`. `create`, `assign`, `move`, and `manage_lists` are `project_manager` or `all_members`. The other actions also accept `assigned_member`.

todo_allowed_actions.description: Whether the current user can perform each to-do action on this project. `bypass` is true when the user can skip these checks.

customFieldsWrite.description: On save, a map of custom field ID to the plain value: text, number, date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), or the enum option ID. An empty value removes the field.

opt_export_columns.name: opt_export_columns
opt_export_columns.description:
Define the optionals columns to be retrieved. Columns used in `opt_group_by` will automatically include their identifiers, such as `*_id` and `*_name`. Some columns will only be displayed depending on the grouping information used in `opt_group_by`.

To include custom fields data, include `custom_field_{id}` replacing the {id} by the properly custom field ID. For custom fields type enum, include `custom_field_{id}_enum_name` to get their label description.

opt_group_by.name: opt_group_by
opt_group_by.description:
Group time data by columns. Use comma-separated list of columns to group by many.

A maximum of 5 groups are allowed. Each group in the response will be displayed as a sublevel.

Beyond of native columns, is allowed grouping by custom fields of type enum, by including `custom_field_{id}` replacing the {id} by the properly custom field ID.

opt_report_template.name: opt_report_template
opt_report_template.description: Templates return grouped rows even when a group is empty. Leave empty for the default. `days` returns every day in the period. `months` returns every month. `users_and_days`, `users_and_weeks`, and `users_and_months` return every user crossed with that period.
